raw_response:
I farm in Quzhou County on the North China Plain, so I would keep to the system I trust most: winter wheat followed by summer maize. That matches my land, my water conditions, and the way I know how to manage risk. I would not spread myself across too many crops, because with my experience and education level, I make better money from a simple rotation I understand well than from chasing a complicated plan. Wheat gives me a steady first harvest, and maize uses the summer heat and rain well after wheat comes off. I would use improved or hybrid seed, put most of my fertilizer into the wheat and maize because those are the crops that reliably pay, irrigate wheat more than maize because spring is often dry, and keep pesticide spraying to a practical level instead of overdoing it. For tillage, I would use rotary tillage because it is familiar, efficient, and fits the way most fields around me are prepared. My goal would be stable yield, controlled costs, and low management risk rather than gambling on something unfamiliar.
